source_read: PMC HTML full text PMC7669776 (Forensic Sci Med Pathol 2020;16(4):680-692; title confirmed in my own tab). Read: every section, Tables 1 to 4 with footnotes, Key points, contributions, availability statements and the reference list; section and paragraph structure checked in the page. Figures 1 (flowchart) and 2 (restraint type by drug) were not viewed, because screenshots of my background tab came back blank earlier in this session; no card value depends on them. The Springer article page (via the DOI) was checked: labelled Review, published 22 August 2020, with no correction, funding or conflict statement. Also read in full: de Boer et al. 2023 (PMC10752912); Freeman et al. 2023 reply with its Appendix Table 1 (PMC10752838); de Boer et al. 2024 (PMC11525397); Freeman et al. 2024 second reply (Springer HTML, 10.1007/s12024-023-00736-w). The critics' Online Resource 1 (a PDF) was not opened. No claims cite this source in this round; card check only.

key_findings.note: Methods has six paragraphs on the page; the coding rules are in the 4th and 5th. The reply's admission is real: the two McDaniel et al. cases were coded AgDS because they were described as 'agitated' and 'delusional'.
1342 - 320 = 1022; 1022 - 941 = 81 = 61 + 20. Table 1 has 61 counted articles (Murphy et al. excluded) summing to 168.
OR 9.86; Woolf 4.53 to 21.47 reproduced. All 15 Woolf intervals in analysis.effect_sizes reproduce from the printed counts.
All eight odds ratios reproduce from the counts (7.41, 10.69, 49.97, 2.33, 0.037, 1.40, 0.18, 1.24).
94 = 104 - 2 - 8 and 43 = 64 - 1 - 20; 94 + 43 = 137, the Table 2 count in key finding 2. The card is right that the paper's 'restraint' here includes sedation.
Odds ratios reproduce (2.66, 1.76, 0.10, 0.61, 0.35, 4.26). See missed: the Results sentence lists the non-significant alcohol and stimulant differences among the significant ones.
The Table 3 odds ratios (alcohol 4.6, marijuana 0.4, other 0.2, none 4.3) also reproduce.
The eight Table 1 articles dated before 2000 sum to 30 cases.

Table 4 recomputed: the 15 ExDS studies give 666 cases and 529 deaths (528 from the studies at 100% plus 1 from Hall); AgDS 148 plus Southall's 5 = 153; data sources 2 police, 7 hospital, 10 post-mortem; 8 describe restraint. Corrected-table arithmetic reproduced: 529 - 71 - 43 + 25 = 440 of 691 (63.7%).
Reference 18 is Vilke et al. 2012 (J Emerg Med), 97 is DeBard et al. 2009 (the ACEP white paper) and 98 is Barnett et al. 2007.

reporting_issues.note: Recomputed: paramedic 0.064 (Woolf 0.025 to 0.165), other 0.28. The authority odds ratios in Table 3 (0.13 and 0.14, printed 0.1 and 0.1) are correct.

In Table 2 the values are rotated: printed Black 1.4 is the 'unknown' value, printed 'other' 0.9 is the Black value (0.89), and '>999.9' belongs to 'other' (no survivors). In Table 3, Black (0.7) is right and 'other' and 'unknown' are swapped.
The abstract also gives 62% (104 of 168) as the share of all cases that were fatal.

No correction is linked on PMC or Springer (both checked). The reply calls the error a minor transcription error in the mortality column, but its table also changes a case count (Strote 2006), a data source (Cole) and Baldwin's year (2016 to 2015), and renames the restraint column 'Restraint status known'.

The reply shows reviewer judgment in two more places: Atherton et al. was included because excited delirium is a keyword, and for O'Halloran and Frank the reviewers judged 20 of 21 cases consistent, where the source said up to 18 could be so read. The intended Byard, Penders and Schiavone papers are references 8, 12 and 15 of the reply.

risk_of_bias.note: Critically low agreed: seven critical items are unmet. AMSTAR 2 applied by analogy is a reasonable choice for a structured search with pooled case analysis (Springer labels the paper a Review). Item 4 is 'no' from the unjustified English-only restriction alone.

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: 1. PICO components in research question and inclusion criteria
7. List of excluded studies with justification (critical)
8. Included studies described in adequate detail
9. Satisfactory risk-of-bias assessment of included studies (critical)
10. Funding sources of included studies reported
12. Impact of risk of bias on pooled results assessed

16. Conflicts of interest and funding reported
risk_of_bias_domains.note: The 2023 reply also carries no conflict statement; see missed.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial agreed; every quoted phrase was checked against the page. On point (6): the 1-in-353,000 figure reproduces only if the 42 tons are US short tons and the upper end of the paper's assumed amount per use is taken (with metric tonnes about 1 in 389,000). The sentence gives no clear source for the roughly 2,700 deaths: it cites a drugabuse.com page for consumption and a federal drug-impaired-driving report after the risk figure. 'Commercial website' is the card's own description of the drugabuse.com reference.

missed: Reporting issue (Discussion, 1st paragraph): the authors call the 'other or unspecified' force category 'less aggressive forms of restraint (i.e. pepper spray, 4-point restraint, etc.)', but the Methods (4th paragraph) define it as also including blunt objects. The '2.5 times' figure is the inverse of Table 3's 0.4.

Reporting issue (Results › Analysis of outcome): the text says drug use differed significantly for most categories and lists alcohol and stimulants alongside cocaine, marijuana and other drugs, but Table 2 gives p = 0.26 and 0.15 for these two. Discussion, 2nd paragraph, says the marijuana and 'other' drug associations held 'regardless of diagnosis', yet no analysis stratified by label is reported.

selection_effects undercounts: by the paper's own reference titles, at least seven Table 1 sources name a death in restraint or restraint asphyxia. Adding Stratton et al. 1995 (2 cases), Rayamane et al. 2015 (2), Morrison and Sadler 2001 (1) and Kunz et al. 2018 (1) to the card's three gives 55 cases (33%), plus one in-custody death (Kennedy and Savard 2017). The critics' own figures for Stratton 2001's non-fatal cases differ (196 in 2023, 194 in 2024), which justifies the card's 'about'.

Interests: the 2023 reply also has no conflict-of-interest statement and gives Freeman's second affiliation as a post-office box in Portland, Oregon. The 2024 consultation declaration is printed under the heading 'Ethics approval and consent to participate'.
